title: EXP-026 — Button Component Recovery Across Ordinary Close/Reopen
objective: Create one new User-scoped classic BuildFromScratch Form `FX_ComponentRecoveryLab01`, record its untouched visible baseline, and perform exactly one native Button creation operation using the verified placement procedure. As required identification setup, assign the component Name `FX_ButtonRecovery01` using only the verified Name-edit portion of the configuration recipe, without changing Caption or unrelated properties. Record exact component Name and the rendered Type label (expected PushButton for the Toolbox Button) before the lifecycle test. Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save to a clean target state, close the target once through its ordinary Form-tab close control, reopen it once through Designer Form-menu recent forms in the same Designer/client, and verify the recorded Name and Type recover unchanged. This is a first observation of UI-level structural component recovery for this bounded sequence, not a complete component-inventory claim or proof of database durability, cache eviction, metadata unloading, Button Caption persistence, backend object identity or other component types.

acceptance_checks.description: Before any target mutation, record inherited visible Forms/dialogs and dirty state without changing them, prove a usable live Mongoose workflow and User editing scope, and use the supported Select Form Name filter with Case Sensitive unchecked and a visible known-existing positive control to prove zero FX_ComponentRecoveryLab01 matches. Any permitted pre-mutation session establishment must preserve inherited state, avoid credential exposure, and be followed by re-proving these guards; otherwise stop blocked.

Perform one target Form creation using the replay-verified EXP-019-R2 fresh-dialog rendered Classic/Build from Scratch selection prefix followed by the separately verified basic-form procedure. Prove Save Template unchecked and the loaded clean target identity by Name FX_ComponentRecoveryLab01 + ScopeType User + ScopeName. Do not claim that the entire composed procedure is already replay-verified.

Before Button placement, capture an inspected untouched post-creation baseline identifying the target Form, User scope, clean state and rendered canvas/component state. Record any supported visible inventory result; a blank canvas or missing visible Button alone does not establish complete component cardinality. If an unexpected existing Button is observed, preserve the state and stop blocked rather than deleting or replacing it.

Perform exactly one native Button creation operation and verify the placed component. Assign Name FX_ButtonRecovery01 using only the verified Name-edit step as identification setup. Capture the exact property-grid/accessibility Name and Type label (expected PushButton for Toolbox Button), with inspected rendered evidence labeled separately. Do not change Caption or unrelated properties, invoke another editor mechanism after failure, or infer total component count from one creation action. If the required FX_ Name cannot be established, stop blocked after bounded read-only inspection.

Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after placement and required Name setup. Prove the selected target Form returns clean and the component retains Name FX_ButtonRecovery01 and the exact Type label recorded in AC-4. No component property changes are permitted after the AC-4 baseline.

Close FX_ComponentRecoveryLab01 exactly once through its ordinary Form-tab close control, with no unsaved-change or unexpected prompt and no explicit unload. Visibly prove the target tab is closed while the same Designer/client and inherited Forms are retained.

Reopen FX_ComponentRecoveryLab01 exactly once through Designer Form-menu recent forms in the same Designer/client. If the entry or required route is unavailable, stop blocked without an alternative reopen path. Verify Name + ScopeType + ScopeName, component Name FX_ButtonRecovery01, exact Type equal to AC-4 (normally PushButton), and clean target state using decisive inspected evidence. Do not infer internal object identity, complete component inventory or Caption persistence.

Final read-only supported case-insensitive Select Form Name-filter evidence must show exactly one FX_ComponentRecoveryLab01; an expired or obstructed read is unresolved, not permission for recovery across the tested boundary. Reconcile one Form creation action, one Button creation operation, the permitted FX_ Name setup, one ordinary Save, one target Form-tab close, one recent-forms reopen, no Caption/unrelated property mutations, no additional Button creation action, no unload/Regenerate, no post-mutation authentication and no inherited-state cleanup. Repository changes must be confined to the EXP-026 record plus evidence/EXP-026/. Classify a successful first execution only as observed UI-level structural recovery for the bounded Name/type comparison.

initial_instruction: Complete AC-1 preflight and preserve inherited dirty Forms/dialogs before target mutation. The record is new and expected to be missing: create it at the declared path rather than repeatedly searching Git. Use the verified creation/placement procedures and only the component configuration recipe's Name step to establish FX_ButtonRecovery01; do not change Caption or perform that recipe's separate Save. Record Toolbox Button versus the observed property-grid Type (normally PushButton). One placement is an action count, not proof of total inventory. Stop blocked if the required Name or prescribed lifecycle route fails; do not try an alternate editor, scripted recovery or reopen route. Report the bounded task result to the coordinator and stop.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261006-162608-kmU9. Rationale: EXP-025 is blocked because the available MCP surface cannot satisfy its required persistent lifecycle-telemetry gate, so the next experiment should not work around that tooling limitation. A small independent learning step is to establish whether a native Button component itself recovers across the already-used weak ordinary Form-tab close/reopen boundary. This builds only on replay-verified prerequisites: basic BuildFromScratch Form creation, native component placement/configuration, and the fresh-dialog classic wizard-selection sequence. It deliberately does not test Button Caption, avoiding overlap with the unresolved/unknown EXP-020 record and the blocked EXP-018 Button-Caption attempt. Structural Button recovery is a useful prerequisite before any later Button-property lifecycle experiment. Draft correction: use an FX_-prefixed component identity, distinguish the visible PushButton Type from Toolbox Button, distinguish one creation action from complete component cardinality, preserve inherited dirty state, and fix the tested reopen path to recent forms. Component Name assignment is required identification setup through the previously verified Name-edit procedure, not Caption testing; its success in the current environment remains a prerequisite to observe, especially given EXP-021-R4's Static Name-edit blocker. Revised draft remains unapproved pending specialist assessment.
